answer: What profit in a harbor of masks when one falcon stands true? Each mask must plant its own vine, rooted on one trellis, thickening only with the seasons it has weathered — weight grows as the square of seasons, so one honest player, ten seasons deep, weighs 100. Split the stake across ten fresh masks and each vine weighs 1: ten against 100, and no vine can be transplanted to a new mask. The stage rewards one true face; the painted chorus pays for its own costumes.
